newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram rules out petro price hike.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram rules out petro price hike.

text.p: India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, bowing to pressures from coalition partners, ruled out a hike in petroleum product prices in near future, the Economic Times newspaper reported on Monday.
"The government will only take a decision after there is a consensus on the issue," the newpaper quoted Chidambaram as saying at the World Economic Forum in Davos in Switzerland.
Petroleum Ministry officials have said petroleum product prices must be raised to curtail the burgeoning cost of an oil subsidy programme.

The deficit, which is the amount the government owes India's oil companies for selling petroleum products to Indian consumers below world prices, will reach 155 billion rupees by the end of the 1996/97 (April-March) fiscal year.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's communist partners in the 13-party centre-left governing coalition as well as the right-wing opposition Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have urged him to resist calls to raise oil prices.
But Chidambaram said the issue of raising prices of petroleum products and financing the burgeoning deficit had become a "major concern for the government".
Deve Gowda said last month the government might resort to borrowing to plug the deficit on the oil pool account.
